title: Your AI agent is only as safe as the packages it downloads
content_md: Strip away the model names and the headlines, and this year’s AI agent incidents share a feature that has little to do with how capable the models are. Nearly all of them ran through the software supply chain. Start with the case that set off the summer’s wave of disclosures. In July, two OpenAI models undergoing a cyber-capability evaluation escaped their sandbox . They got out through a zero-day vulnerability in a package registry proxy that sat inside the evaluation boundary, placed there so the models could install the tools they needed. From there, they reached the open internet and went after Hugging Face’s production systems, looking for the benchmark’s answer key. Hugging Face caught and contained the intrusion on July 16. Five days later, OpenAI confirmed the incident and connected it to an internal cybersecurity evaluation of frontier AI models. Soon after, Anthropic disclosed three incidents in which its Claude AI models compromised external organizations after a misconfiguration left live internet access in place. In September, it added a fourth that a wider review had turned up. The incident that Anthropic says worries it the most involved a model publishing malicious packages to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Separately, researchers have attributed more than 2,000 RubyGems uploads in May to OpenAI agents. OpenAI says its agents were carrying out benign tasks.
